caption: A tennis ball is thrown hard against a brick wall and bounces back the way it came.

sa.check: A tennis ball is thrown hard at a brick wall.
It bounces back the way it came.
The throw and the strike come first, then the rebound.

pc.expect: The ball leaves the wall back along its incoming line and travels slower than it arrived.
pc.fail: The ball leaves the wall quicker than it arrived; or it drops straight down at the wall without coming back; or it carries on sideways along the face of the wall.

pc.expect: The ball meets the face of the wall and stays outside it.
pc.fail: The ball passes into the brickwork; or it sinks part way in and then comes back out; or it sticks to the wall and hangs there.

pc.expect: The ball squashes briefly where it meets the brick and springs back round, and the wall is unmarked.
pc.fail: The ball stays flattened after the bounce; or it splatters like a wet lump against the brick; or the wall dents or bulges where the ball hits it.

pc.expect: After the rebound the ball's path bends downward toward the ground.
pc.fail: The ball climbs steadily after the bounce and keeps climbing; or it holds one flat line away from the wall to the edge of the frame; or it hangs in the air after the rebound.

pc.expect: One ball and one wall are there throughout.
pc.fail: The ball vanishes at the wall or a second one appears; or the ball turns into another object at the bounce; or a piece of the wall disappears where the ball strikes.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The ball's colour, the brick pattern and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The ball changes colour at the bounce; or the brick courses shift between frames; or the scene beside the wall rearranges.
